title: Singapore DayOne Data Centers secures $3.7B financing package from 7 lenders
key_facts: A consortium of seven lenders arranged expanded multi-currency financing of RM15 billion (US$3.7 billion) for DayOne to support its data centre platform in Johor, Malaysia.
The lenders are CIMB, Credit Agricole CIB, DBS, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB, acting as mandated lead arrangers, bookrunners and joint coordinators.
The new money is a US$2.4 billion offshore term loan facility plus a RM5.5 billion Murabahah facility.
With the RM15 billion secured in 2025, the financing platform now stands at RM30 billion, a joint statement from the lenders said on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026.
DayOne was established in 2022, is headquartered in Singapore and operates in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Finland and Spain.
DayOne filed for a proposed Nasdaq initial public offering on 6 Oct 2026, planning to raise as much as US$5 billion at a potential US$20 billion valuation.
Malaysia's data centre supply capacity is projected to reach 4.2 to 6.1 gigawatts by 2030, based on Boston Consulting Group data.
quote_evidence: A consortium of seven lenders has arranged expanded multi-currency financing of RM15 billion (US$3.7 billion) for DayOne to support the continued development of its data centre platform in Johor, Malaysia.
Together with the RM15 billion multi-currency financing secured in 2025, the financing platform now stands at RM30 billion, a joint statement from the lenders noted on Tuesday (Oct 13).

The Singapore-headquartered firm most recently filed for a proposed Nasdaq initial public offering in the US on Oct 6, with plans to raise as much as US$5 billion, with a potential valuation of US$20 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: Banks are still lending heavily for AI data center building in Southeast Asia.
